newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW sees A$700 mln Sydney harbour-front project.
newsitem.headline: NSW sees A$700 mln Sydney harbour-front project.

text.p: The New South Wales state government announced plans for a A$700 million redevelopment of the eastern side of Sydney's Darling Harbour that would be partly completed by the 2000 Olympics.
New South Wales Ports Minister Carl Scully said the project on a five hectare site north of the Sydney Acquarium behind Darling Harbour wharves nine and ten would include;
* a 500 room hotel and 330 serviced apartments,
* a 50,000 square metre office building, and,
* assorted retail and recreational buildings adjacent to the waterfront.
The project would also include two new ferry wharves and a second point for ferry services for the central business district, Scully said in statement.
The Darling Harbour Passenger Terminal would be relocated from wharf 10 to wharf eight, he said.
"A master plan for the redevelopment will be presented to the Central Sydney Planning Committee next month, with proposals to be sought from the private sector shortly after."
